hints: Look at the shape of the $force / \text{N}$ against $extension / \text{m}$ curve: a steep near-straight start followed by a long flatter stretch to breaking.
Connect that shape to behaviour: the first part is reversible elastic stretching up to the elastic limit, the second long part is permanent plastic stretching.
Connect work done to area: stretching to breaking needs the area under the whole curve from $0$ extension to the breaking extension, not just the elastic or just the plastic part.
walkthrough: Identify the given graph: $force / \text{N}$ on the vertical axis against $extension / \text{m}$ on the horizontal axis, drawn from $0$ to the breaking point.

State the rule for regions: the elastic region is the initial part where extension is small and largely proportional to force, and the wire would return to zero; the plastic region follows after the elastic limit where large permanent extension occurs.
State the rule for energy: work done to stretch the wire is the area under the force-extension graph, given by $W = \text{area under } F \text{ versus } x$.
Apply to breaking: because the wire is stretched until it breaks, the area must be summed over both the elastic and the plastic extensions, i.e. the whole area from $0$ to the final extension.
Check the options: only the graph with elastic first, plastic second, and shading under the entire curve satisfies all three labels. This is option D
